off_list.why: The 'Exhibit 6' (6A–6E) and 'Exhibit 1 rifle' that Sgt. Faumuina read aloud on Day 4 are the ATF firearms report's OWN item numbers, not the court's State's-Exhibit numbers: at `day4.txt` 05:30:32 counsel asks to 'scroll back up to show the exhibit list. Number 6, what is Exhibit 6?' and the witness reads 'Exhibit 6 consists of…' from the report's p. 2; CR-E15 §2 transcribes the report's face — 'Exhibits examined, as listed: (1) one Mauser, model 98, 30-06 … rifle … (6) one bullet jacket fragment and four lead fragments, designated 6A through 6E'; CR-E20:24 states the State's map 'does not govern … ATF's or the FBI's internal item numbering'. On the hearing record the State's numbers 1 and 6 are other things: State's Exhibit 1 is a photograph of the UVU campus area offered through Officer Bagley on Day 1 (`day1.txt` 00:57:15–00:57:22, 'fair and accurate depiction of this area of UVU campus'), and State's Exhibit 6/6.1 is a Day-1 witness video/statement ruled on under Rule 1102 and UCJA 4-202.02 (`day1.txt` 04:46:57, 04:49:33, 05:01:39 'state's exhibit 6.1. Oh, I'm sorry, six'). So SEC-E02's 'State's Exhibit 6' names the wrong owner in a finding (F-112), the resolution (§4.4) and §1. Confidence High (three independent primary/library sources agree). The replacement deliberately does NOT write 'State's Exhibit 32's item 6': the report's identity with State's Exhibit 32 is an inference (CR-E20 F-4 High / CR-E15 F-139 Medium-high) and a flat identity would be a C-38 carrier; the discipline word 'firearms' satisfies CR-E20 Rule 1 (C-32). The v1.1 revision row (line 183, 'Exhibit 6's wound-recovered') is RECORD — leave it and name it in the new row.
